hypotheses.name: H1: an unprotected late read of game RAM (texture/CLUT image data outside the copies) sees step k+1 data on the deck
hypotheses.mechanism: In two-area ME turns the walk of picture k runs while the main CPU runs the logic step and the next drawing step, and it may finish as late as the second hook after its own (xl_psp.c:1840-1844, MW_HOOK). The walk reads from the arena copy only the tags, the cnt data and the ref'd non-image data. Image data outside xc_keep (xlme.c:186; marks cut from rb at xlme.c:196-205) is read from main RAM at walk time. The GS map also reads upload and CLUT bytes lazily through m->ram, either at the upload's end (rec_ident, gsup2.c:408) or when a texture is decoded (rec_bytes, gsup2.c:230), and these go to xm_ram (xlme.c:345), which is the current record's view or RAM. If step k+1 rewrites such bytes, the frame converts k+1 texels or palette entries.
hypotheses.evidence_for: lchk4 was run with gl24-era settings. It never covered gl26's cut b in every block from vb 24,000 or TWO=1 in every ME turn. The ME is busy walking for 84% of a deck ME turn on the PSP (gl26 log /home/claude/runs/gl26/log.txt:2861, walks 7570 of 9018 ms), so late reads do happen there. The known case (C7, deck start) is real: the late emulator runs reproduce it at vb 26,007.
hypotheses.evidence_against: EXPERIMENT [C, emulator]: the gl27 code and cfg with every ME-turn walk held until the main CPU waited for it (the latest the code allows: 49 of 50 walks per deck turn released by the MW_HOOK wait). All 2,679 frame digests from vb 26,000 to 31,959 equal the x86 twin out_g22b.log, including every frame of 30,500-31,400. The only difference is vb 26,007, which is the known C7 case and is identical in the unstressed control. The digest hashes the texture bytes and palettes (gelive.c:508-521), and the 26,007 positive control shows the method detects late reads.
hypotheses.psp_only_why: PPSSPP's stand-in thread normally walks at the hook's probe or at the main thread's sleeps, and lchk said the emulator 'cannot show it'. The stress run forced the PSP's worst-case lateness on the emulator, and it still showed no difference on the deck.
hypotheses.test: Done on the emulator (stress, see experiments). The decisive PSP test is cfg-only: rerun gl27 with MGS2_GL_DIG=30500:31400 (today's window 31,561-31,959 lies past the PSP route's end at 31,400, so no PSP run has ever printed deck digests) and run tools/emucmp.py on the PSP log against build_gl19/x86/out_g22b.log. Equal digests in the ME turns clear every ME-side input read.
hypotheses.fix: If PSP digests differ in ME turns: copy the read ranges at transfer end (an xc_keep entry), or give the GS map 'own' bytes at upload end. A copy of all upload bytes was tried as gl25b and changed the picture, so the copy needs the map's lazy reads to go through a fixed copy and not through the current record's view. As a stopgap, set MGS2_ME_PIC_TWO=0 on the deck.

hypotheses.name: H2: a transient mid-step write (changed and put back within a step) read by the ME at an intermediate moment
hypotheses.mechanism: The game might rebuild a texture or CLUT buffer in RAM every step (clear, then fill), ending with the same bytes. Endpoint checks (lchk4, and the H1 stress, which reads at the end) cannot see that. The real ME reads at arbitrary moments in the logic step and could pick up a half-built buffer, showing as black patches that come and go.
hypotheses.evidence_for: The symptom (black, flickering, shadow-like) fits a cleared texture. lchk's README names this blind spot ('an endpoint check cannot see a byte changed and put back inside one step').
hypotheses.evidence_against: EXPERIMENT [C, emulator]: the loop thread ran above the main thread (MGS2_ME_PIC_PRI=1), and each walk was held for a deterministic 0-40 ms after the hook, then walked at high priority mid-step. All 50 deck walks per ME turn were released by the timer. Result: 2,680/2,680 frame digests from 26,000 to 31,959 equal the twin. Moments later than 40 ms after the hook were not sampled.
hypotheses.psp_only_why: Only the real ME reads concurrently at arbitrary instants. The emulator's thread reads at its scheduling points.
hypotheses.test: The PSP digest window run as in H1 is decisive. On the emulator, rerun build_bk_late_mid with the timer range widened to 0-120 ms (the deck step pair is about 52 ms on the PSP).
hypotheses.fix: Same as H1: copy the affected source at transfer end, or wait for the walk before the logic step's writes (TWO=0).

hypotheses.name: H3: ME D-cache staleness or incoherence on its reads of main RAM
hypotheses.mechanism: The ME reads game RAM, the queue, the log and the thinning slot through its own write-back cache. A missing invalidate, an incomplete whole-cache write-back+invalidate, or a main-CPU dirty line not written back before the post would feed the walk stale or old bytes.
hypotheses.evidence_for: Hardware-only by nature: PPSSPP has one coherent memory, so the emulator can never show it. It would hit only in ME turns.
hypotheses.evidence_against: By inspection [C], every read path is covered. The walk starts with XME_C_ALL (xme.c:58), the queue entry is invalidated before it is read (xme.c:161), and the REC copy invalidates its extents and source bytes or does a whole-cache op at 16 KB or more (xme.c:20-30, 38). FILL invalidates the log entries (xme.c:45), THIN the slot (xme.c:138), and SYNC/STOP write back the whole cache (xme.c:170). The main CPU calls sceKernelDcacheWritebackAll before every post's head++ (xl_psp.c:1277 mq_post) and write-back+invalidate after SYNC (xl_psp.c:1801). hle_me_dwbinv_all does index op 0x14 twice per 64-byte index over 8 KB, which fits a 16 KB 2-way cache (hle_me.h:108-116; size per me_picture_study.md:79 [S]). hle_me_dinval rounds out to whole lines (hle_me.h:96-100), but the ME never writes game RAM, the extents or the log, so dropping a partial line loses nothing.
hypotheses.psp_only_why: Two non-coherent caches exist only on the real PSP.
hypotheses.test: The PSP digest window run as in H1: a stale input changes the ME's digests. Optional code switch for one PSP run: make xme_cache's INV always do XME_C_ALL (XME_C_BIG 0) and add an XME_C_ALL before each record in xme_walk. If the marks vanish only with that, it is H3.
hypotheses.fix: Whole-cache invalidate at each record, or read game RAM through the uncached alias (0x40000000|addr) in xm_ram/xv_at for RAM parts.

hypotheses.name: H4: ME output not yet in RAM, or overwritten, while the GE reads it (GE2 overlap in ME turns)
hypotheses.mechanism: With GE2=1 (two frames on the GE side), the ME starts frame k+1 at the same hook that listed frame k (xme.c:115-126) and keeps writing the texture pool, the other frame memory and the GS map. Those dirty lines leave the ME's cache at random moments while the GE draws list k. Frame k's data must be fully written back before listed++ (the XME_C_ALL at xme.c:112), and nothing written for k+1 may share memory the GE still reads for k. tk_guard keeps the texture slots, fm[2]/fl[2] double the arena and list, and mq_lines checks whole-line placement. A gap in any of these (a shared palette or texture table, a pool slot reused despite the guard, GEFAST's ge_done from the GE interrupt releasing a slot early) would show as wrong texels or palettes for one frame.
hypotheses.evidence_for: It hits ME turns only: main turns set XS(mq)->ge2=0 (xl_psp.c:1819) and walk at transfer end. That fits 'come and go every few seconds' (alternating 100-vblank blocks). It is PSP-only: PPSSPP's GE, memory and caches leave no such overlap. Shots cannot show it, because the shot path drains the loop and waits for the GE. Digest equality cannot rule it out either: the ME computes the digest from its own cached view before the write-back.
hypotheses.evidence_against: By design, the texture guard, double frame memory and hook write-back cover the known shared state [C xme.c:112,119-123]. gl26 and gl27 shots and hashes are exact. No concrete unguarded buffer was found in this lens's reading.
hypotheses.psp_only_why: The GE draws concurrently with ME writes only on hardware. The emulator's GE is effectively synchronous and its memory coherent.
hypotheses.test: Cfg-only owner eye test on the deck, vb 30,500-31,400: MGS2_ME_PIC_GE2=0 (or GE2=2 for alternate ME turns as an A/B) and separately MGS2_ME_PIC_GEFAST=0. If the marks go with GE2=0 while TWO stays 1, it is this. Add MGS2_GL_DIG=30500:31400 in the same run: equal digests plus visible marks points to output or GE-side causes, not input reads.
hypotheses.fix: Keep GE2=0 on the deck, or before xm_begin of frame k+1 add a whole-cache write-back plus a check that every buffer frame k's list references (tdata, tpal, aux, the pool slots) is untouched until ge_done passes k.

facts: [C ge/xme.c:58] xme_walk calls XME_C_ALL (the whole ME D-cache written back and invalidated) once at the start of each walk. There is no invalidate between records inside a walk.

[C ge/xme.c:31-41, 20-30] An XE_REC copy (xm_fill from fc.mem/fc.spr into the arena) runs when the ME reaches the entry. It first invalidates the record's extents and their source bytes by range, or does a whole-cache op at 16 KB or more (XME_C_BIG). Early copies (now 0) are corrected at XE_FILL by laying the main CPU's guard log over them (xme.c:42-52, log invalidated at :45).

[C ge/xme.c:112] At a hook, after xm_end and xm_list, the ME writes back its whole cache before listed++. With GE2 it then begins frame k+1 in the same entry (xme.c:115-126) while the GE may still draw k. tk_guard keeps the textures in use since frame k's start; the two frame memories and lists alternate (fm_k).
[C ge/xme.c:161, 138, 170] The queue entry is invalidated before it is read, the thinning slot before gl_thin, and SYNC/STOP write back the whole cache after the entry.

[C psp/xl_psp.c:1277] In mode 4, mq_post calls sceKernelDcacheWritebackAll before every head++ (REC, FILL, WALK, HOOK, THIN). Game RAM is in RAM as of each post, but the main CPU's later writes for step k+1 reach RAM whenever its cache evicts them.

[C psp/xl_psp.c:1801, 1819] At a hand-over to a main turn, the ME runs SYNC (whole-cache write-back) and then the main CPU does a write-back+invalidate. Main turns set ge2=0 and walk each transfer from RAM as it ends: no late reads and no GE2 overlap in main turns.

[C psp/xme_me.c:45-50; hle_me.h:96-116] On the ME, XME_C_ALL = hle_me_dwbinv_all (cache 0x14 twice per 64-byte index over 8 KB, a 16 KB 2-way cache [S me_picture_study.md:79]). XME_C_INV = hle_me_dinval (hit-invalidate 0x19, rounded out to whole lines) + sync. The ME reads game RAM through its cached kseg0 view; only the XmeSh words and the results go uncached (xme.h:86-87).

[C ge/xlme.c:186, 196-205] What the walk reads from game RAM instead of the copy is image data (the XL_IMG marks) outside xc_keep = {0x12c0000-0x1430000, 0x1ed0000-0x1ee0000}. Tags, cnt data and ref'd non-image data are copied into the arena.

[C ge/gsup2.c:230-236, 408-412, 976-994] The GS map keeps each host->local upload as its EE source address and reads the bytes lazily through m->ram: for the identity key at the upload's end, and again whenever a texture or CLUT is decoded, possibly a later frame. m->ram = xm_ram (ge/xlme.c:341-346): the current record's view (copy or RAM), or plain RAM outside walks (for example during an XE_HOOK). Every texel and palette byte not in xc_keep is therefore read from game RAM at the ME's own time.

[C ge/gelive.c:508-521] The frame digest covers the batches, vertices, data, the list's aux bytes, and every texture's converted texels (tdata) and palette (tpal). A late texture or CLUT read changes it. The ME computes it from its own (cached) view before the hook write-back.

[C grep of ge/*.c] The translator and converters read guest memory only through the view or ram callbacks (xlive.c:10, 22; xlme.c lw_q/lw_tp/xv_at). No converter reads game RAM directly. fx_thin_scan reads game RAM only on the main CPU (xl_psp.c:1787) and passes ranges to the ME through the slot.
[C runs/gl22-26 log.txt] Every PSP cfg so far has MGS2_GL_DIG=31561:31959 but the route ends at vblanks 31,400, so no PSP run has ever printed frame digests; there are 0 'picture: vb N buffer' lines.

[C runs/gl26/log.txt:2861-3011] PSP deck ME turns (100 vb) last 8.3-9.4 s, of which the walks take 6.2-8.3 s. The ME is walking for most of the turn, so the walks do overlap the main CPU's next steps on hardware.

[C build_bk_late/emu/log.txt BK_LATE lines] On the emulator with the walk held until the main CPU waits for it, the deck releases 49 of 50 walks per ME turn at the MW_HOOK wait (the latest point allowed) and 1 at SYNC.

[C emulator] Frame vb 26,007 (deck start, C7's known late read) has digest e31f3864397c0603 when the loop thread runs below the main thread (MGS2_ME_PIC_PRI=0, the gl27 default; stress or not) and fb85e0d7b97c0603 = the twin when it runs above it (PRI=1). The list digest dfea776eb7eb22a1 is equal in all, so only texture or palette bytes differ. Earlier emulator checks missed this because their digest window started at 31,561.

[I] The PSP's late reads see a mix of step-k and step-k+1 bytes, depending on which main-CPU dirty lines were evicted. Any byte that differs at the endpoint would already differ in the stress run, so the stress run bounds the endpoint case. Transient (changed and put back) writes are bounded only by the 0-40 ms mid-step sampling.

hypotheses.name: H1 (lens: no window found): ME frame N+1 writes overwrite a GE-side buffer that frame N's list still reads (frame memory, list, aux, vertices, pool textures, CLUTs)
hypotheses.mechanism: With GE2=1 the ME begins frame N+1 while the GE still draws N. ge/xme.c:116-122: when two=1, the begin waits until listed-released<=1, then flips fm_k and calls gb_arena on the other frame memory and p->gxl=fl[fm_k]. So N+1 is built in gl_vol/gl_vol2, whichever N is not using. The texture cache also guards N's textures. ge/texcache.c:131/143 evicts only entries with frame < c->frame-1 && frame < guard. The guard is tk_guard(tk_fb) (ge/xme.c:121), and tk_fb is the tk frame at N's begin. Palettes come from the same pool, under the same rule. A GE list only points at its own frame memory (list words, aux, arena vertices and data: ge/gelist.c addr_cmd and aux_get), at pool texels and palettes (texture() :116-139), and at VRAM FB0/FB1/ZB.
hypotheses.evidence_for: None found. Main turns are fully serial: XS->ge2=0 (xl_psp.c:1819), and each begin waits until listed-released<=0 through mq_wait_self->mq_service/mq_ge_finish (xl_psp.c:1349-1356). Only ME turns overlap, which would fit 'come and go' if a race existed.
hypotheses.evidence_against: [C] Emulator experiment bk_gebuf, vb 24,000-31,400, 3,522 lists. It hashed each list's 2 MB frame memory (list block and arena apart), every pool texture (first 8 rows, and all TSIZE rows) and every CLUT the list loads, once when the main CPU first saw the result and again when its list was let go. The GE was held busy 25 ms after each submit and the callback release was off, so the loop thread built frame N+1 while N was in flight. Overlap was real: 'begun while the GE drew the frame before' was 41-50 per ME turn. Result: list block 0 changes, arena 0, palettes 0, texture first-8-rows 0. TSIZE-row windows changed 3 times (vb 26082, 26820, 27204, all ME turns); none was on the walk window 30,500-31,400, and see H2. Code review of fm alternation, results ring (XME_NRES 4), tk_guard and ge_done found no gap.
hypotheses.psp_only_why: PPSSPP runs a list at submit (sceGuFinish -> UpdateStallAddr), so later writes cannot reach it. The emulator check removed that difference by holding the GE 25 ms and still found nothing.
hypotheses.test: cfg-only PSP run of gl27 with MGS2_ME_PIC_GE2=0 and MGS2_ME_PIC_GEFAST=0, TWO left at 1. The ME then never writes while the GE draws. Marks still seen means GE-side lifetimes are excluded on the PSP too. Emulator: rerun build_bk_gebuf (keep MGS2_BK_FROM=24000) after any change to xme.c or texcache.c.
hypotheses.fix: None needed on current evidence. If the GE2=0 run clears the marks, keep GE2=0 and look at H2/H3.

hypotheses.name: H2: GE reads texels past a pool texture's stored rows (TSIZE is a power of two; storage is h+1 rows rounded to 8), into neighbouring pool memory the ME is rewriting
hypotheses.mechanism: texconv.c geomx (:86-101): for clamp axes the stored rows are (h+1+7)/8*8 and bw is (w+1) rounded, while TSIZE0 is p2(w) x p2(h) (gelist.c:132). With GU_CLAMP (twrap 1) the GE clamps at the power-of-two edge, not the stored edge. A tap past row h+1 reads the next pool allocation. Under GE2 that memory can be a texture or palette the ME is converting for frame N+1 while N is drawn (tk_alloc / p_alloc into freed runs).
hypotheses.evidence_for: [C] In bk_gebuf the TSIZE-row window of 3 textures changed while their list was in flight, all in ME turns: 0b681900 at vb 26082 (4,096-byte window) and 0b7df000 at vb 26820 and 27204 (77,824-byte window). Their first 8 rows were unchanged each time, so the change lay past the stored part. Such content would be timing-dependent and show only in ME turns on the PSP.
hypotheses.evidence_against: The texconv.c comment says bilinear taps reach at most one texel past a REGION_CLAMP edge on every deck draw (gsref), and the extra edge row is stored. No change of this kind occurred in 30,500-31,400, where the marks are seen. Texture conversions are rare on the route: gl26 log line 3081 shows 1,345 conversions and 2,029 evictions in the whole run. The pattern does not fit marks that are frequent on the deck.
hypotheses.psp_only_why: PPSSPP draws at submit, before the ME thread writes the neighbour. Also, past the stored rows PPSSPP reads whatever is there at that moment.
hypotheses.test: Emulator variant: pad each pool allocation to tbw*th (or add 8 guard rows filled with magenta) in tk_alloc for convert(). Then compare emulator digests and pictures; PPSSPP shows a magenta edge if UVs reach past the stored rows. On the PSP: the same padding build, and see if the marks change.
hypotheses.fix: Store rows up to th (and bw up to tw) for clamp textures, or set the GE's clamp to the stored size by drawing with a scaled TSIZE. This costs some pool memory (budget 2,352 KB, peak 2,352 KB in gl26).

hypotheses.name: H3 (outside lens, the strongest PSP-only + ME-turn mechanism seen): the TWO walk reads game RAM (image data left in RAM, outside its copies) while the main CPU runs the next step. It sees mid-step transient values, or a mix of old and new lines because the main CPU's write-back D-cache lets lines out at random times
hypotheses.mechanism: With TWO=1 (gl25 two-area turns, gl26 every ME turn) xme_walk (ge/xme.c:53-70) runs during logic step k+1. It reads texture source bytes left in game RAM: xm_plan cuts the image marks out of the copy except xc_keep (ge/xlme.c:186). The main CPU's game writes since its last post sit in its cache and reach RAM at eviction times. The ME's dwbinv_all happens only at the walk's start.
hypotheses.evidence_for: Seen from gl26 and probably gl25, which is when TWO overlap began. lchk4 compared that RAM only at hook points, so a transient write mid-step (cleared then redrawn, or decompressed in place) passes it. The emulator loop thread runs only while the main thread blocks, at hook waits, so it can never read mid-step. Shots: the deck shots 30502 and 31114 are both in main turns (vb/100 odd) [C: runs/gl26 shot_30500.bmp, shot_31112.bmp]. Shots have therefore never sampled an ME-turn deck frame.
hypotheses.evidence_against: Not in this lens; no direct evidence of transient writes. lchk4 found only vb 20,692 and 26,008 changed over two hooks.
hypotheses.turn_type: ME turns only (the ones with TWO on)
hypotheses.psp_only_why: True concurrency plus cache write-back timing exist only on the PSP. On the emulator the walk runs at hook waits and sees end-of-step RAM.
hypotheses.test: cfg-only PSP run: gl27 with MGS2_ME_PIC_TWO=0 (GE2/GEFAST unchanged). Marks gone means a late read. Or TWO=2, so only alternate ME turns have the overlap, if the owner can tell turns apart. Emulator: a variant that forces the loop thread to run the walk mid-step (e.g. sceKernelDelayThread in xlive_chk_dma) plus an lchk-style compare of the marked ranges at several mid-step points.
hypotheses.fix: Copy the image ranges the walk reads (extend xc_keep to the deck's dynamic texture sources), or end the walk before the main CPU writes them (TWO off on the deck).

hypotheses.name: H4 (outside lens, competing deterministic cause): real GE hardware draws deck triangles that cross the near plane differently from PPSSPP (CLIP off for df0 and lit batches)
hypotheses.mechanism: gelist.c:509 enables C_CLIP only for GERK_XFORMF effect batches. Terrain (xf_draw, lit_draw) is drawn with CLIP 0 after sceGuDisable(GU_CLIP_PLANES) (xl_psp.c:261). Real GE behaviour for vertices behind or near the eye differs from PPSSPP's, which can give black spikes or marks that come and go as the camera moves.
hypotheses.evidence_for: The marks are on the deck terrain while Snake walks, so camera and terrain geometry change. The emulator would not show them.
hypotheses.evidence_against: It would appear in main turns too, and in any build since gl18, while the owner first saw it in gl26/gl25. The deck shots (main turns) look normal, though they may simply have caught a 'gone' moment.
hypotheses.psp_only_why: GE hardware clip and guard-band behaviour is not emulated exactly by PPSSPP.
hypotheses.test: cfg-only PSP run with the ME picture off (MGS2_ME_PIC_ME=0, or no turns), so every frame is a main-CPU frame with no overlap. Marks still seen means H4-like and deterministic. A PSP shot taken at the moment the owner sees them settles it.
hypotheses.fix: Enable C_CLIP for xf_draw/lit_draw on the deck, or cull triangles with w<=near on the converter side.

facts: [C] GE-visible memory is exactly: frame memory gl_vol (volatile block, 0x08600000 on PSP) and gl_vol2 (memalign 64, 2,048 KB), each holding arena 1,696 KB plus list/aux 352 KB (xl_psp.c:240-251, gelive.h:124-127); texture pool gl_pool (2,688 KB, 64-byte units, texcache.c tk_pool); the direct list gl_dl (written uncached by sceGuStart); VRAM FB0 0x000000, FB1 0x088000, ZB 0x110000 (16-bit), TXT 0x154000 (xl_psp.c:168-171). No render-to-texture or VRAM scratch: GS render targets are drawn untextured (texcache.c TK_RT; gl26: 181 lookups). Frame-buffer textures (kind 2, gelive.c:41-48) read the draw buffer (depth blur, cut_draw) or the other buffer (motion trail; the trail is cut on the deck by HALF_CYCLE b).

[C] gelist.c addr_cmd / aux_get / texture(): every VADDR/IADDR points into the list's own frame memory (F->v, F->d, aux); TBP/CBP point into the pool or VRAM; the clear sprite is in aux; the depth clear is in every list (gelist.c:579, CLEAR (1|4)<<8).

[C] Two frames in flight only in ME turns: ge/xme.c:116 two = XS->ge2 && fm[1]; begin waits while listed-released > two, then flips fm_k (:122). hypotheses.name: H1: The coarse per-frame depth map leaves the subtractive deck decal within 1 GE depth unit of the deck, and the real GE's depth rounding drops it in patches
hypotheses.mechanism:
[C] The Tanker deck is drawn as a base mesh followed by a df0 decal or overlay mesh. The overlay uses blend (2,0,0,1) = (0-Cs)*As+Cd, which gelist.c blend() case 0x42 maps to G_REVSUB with dst G_FIX fb=W. It has the same world matrix and strip layout as the base but its own vertices, lying a few world units above the deck. Examples: batch 788 over 787 at vb 31112, and 709/711 over 701/703 at 30930. It is depth-tested GEQUAL against the deck, with ZTMAP in gelist.c gx_batch:478-527.

[C] gx_depth_map (ge/gelist.c:538-546, called from ge/xlme.c xm_list) builds a per-frame z scale from f->map_lo/map_hi (gelive.c gl_end, xconv.c xc_zr). Vertices nearer than the near plane are clamped to 16,773,120 (xconv.c:84-120 xc_zr_end), so once any vertex crosses the near plane, map_hi jumps to ~16.77M. The 16-bit range then spans ~29k..16.77M Z24, about 287 Z24 per GE step (it was ~3.3 Z24 per step before vb 30850).

[C] From the GER replays, the decal's margin above the deck shrinks:
- 30620 (fine map): median 23.9 GE units.
- 30930: median 0.20 units.
- 31112: median 0.88 units.

At 31112 the vertex z values are 708.97 for the base and 709.52 for the overlay (viewport z scale -30835.5, offset 30850.5). At 30930 they are 358.71 and 358.89. 25k-50k overlay pixels are within 1 unit.

[I] With a sub-unit margin, whether a decal pixel passes GEQUAL depends on the rasterizer's exact z interpolation and rounding:
- Base and overlay have different vertex positions, so their interpolated z can cross in patches.
- Where the decal fails, the pixel shows the undarkened deck.
- Where the decal's own strips overlap each other (several subtractive layers), the decal can apply twice. A doubled (0-Cs)*As subtract drives the deck towards black, which gives black blotches.

The patches move as the camera moves, and the map alternates between frames during 30850-31070, so they flicker and come and go.
hypotheses.evidence_for:
[C] The symptom window (vb ~30500-31400) overlaps the coarse-map period exactly: alternating 1M-5M versus 9.5M-16.77M from 30850 to 31070, then ~29k..16,773,120 from 31070 to 31709 (twin out_g22b.log xlive gb map lines).

[C] zfight2: rounding-sensitive pixels (within 1 unit of another mesh's depth) go from 376 at 30620 to 3,600-4,100 at 30930-31290, with 20-26k within 2 units. They are dominated by the subtractive overlay over its base.

[C] zfight3 margin numbers are as given above.

[C] The overlay is a darkening (REVSUB) pass, so its misbehaviour produces dark or black marks, matching 'shadow-like'.

The real GE would need non-monotonic interpolation, for example per-span fixed-point z deltas with limited fractional bits, or a different setup for the decal's triangles.

UNKNOWN: the real GE's z interpolation precision; I have no hardware data.

[C] The PSP shots at 30500 and 31112 (gl26, main turns) show no terrain black clusters either, so no captured PSP frame shows the marks yet.

- PPSSPP softgpu truncates vertex z to u16 and interpolates per pixel in float before truncating. That ordering is monotonic and keeps the decal in front.
- The real GE rasterizer uses fixed-point edge and z deltas whose rounding can reverse a sub-unit ordering in places. This is UNKNOWN until measured.

hypotheses.mechanism: With GE2 (gl23) the ME begins frame N+1 (xme_hook begin: fm_k ^= 1, gb_arena, tk_guard(x->tk_fb)) while the GE draws frame N. GEFAST's ge_fin_cb sets XS(mq)->ge_done = mq_subm from the GE interrupt. If anything frame N's list points to is written by the ME for N+1, the GE samples the new bytes. Black texels are likely, because the texture pool and the frame memory start memset to 0. Examples: a pool entry dropped despite the guard, a palette entry, aux, or a line shared with another region.
hypotheses.evidence_for: Black marks that come and go fit wrong texels on some draws in some frames. This is the defining PSP-only overlap: PPSSPP runs the list at sceGuFinish, so the GE never overlaps the ME's next frame. It is ME-turns only, since main turns set XS(mq)->ge2=0 and wait for the GE at each begin. The 3 PSP deck shots (29,500, 30,500, 31,112) were all taken in main turns, and the shot path (xl_psp_gl_vblank: mq_drain, mq_service, mq_ge_finish) drains the loop, so the GE draws the shot frame with the ME idle. Shots can therefore never show this.
hypotheses.evidence_against: [C, code read] I found no shared memory. Lists, aux, the clear quad and the strip index buffers are all in the list block of fl[k] (gelist.c aux_get, lines 216, 576). Batches and vertices are in fm[k]'s arena. Textures and palettes are pool entries. make_room and the line-131 drop both keep entries with frame >= guard, and the guard covers every entry touched while frame N was built (touch sets e->frame = c->frame >= tk_fb+1). gl_vol2 and gl_pool are memalign(64). The ME's dwbinv_all before listed++ writes back whole lines whose unchanged bytes equal RAM.
hypotheses.psp_only_why: Only real hardware has the GE drawing for about 22-27 ms while the ME writes.
hypotheses.test: PSP run with GE2=2, GEFAST=2 and TWO=2 under TURN=300 (an on block and an off block of ME turns in the walk), plus live captures of the finished buffer at gl_show without draining. Dark clusters in on-block captures, none in off-block or main-turn captures, with digests equal to the twin, means H2. Container side: add a debug fence that, at each GE finish, compares a hash of frame N's pool entries and list block taken at xm_list with the same hash taken at ge_noted. On the emulator it must always agree; on the PSP a mismatch names the region.
hypotheses.fix: MGS2_ME_PIC_GE2=0 (cfg; gives back gl23's gain). Or find the region with the fence and guard it, for example by delaying p_alloc reuse of anything freed while a list is in flight.

hypotheses.name: H3 ME data-cache coherence hole (the GE sees RAM different from what the ME computed)
hypotheses.mechanism: The ME's frame or texture writes are not all in RAM when listed moves, or the ME reads a stale clean line of memory the main CPU wrote after the ME cached it. Everything goes through xme_cache, which is skipped when x->cache == 0. The ME reads the ctx header (w_me, clk_me) cached while idle in the main CPU's turns, while the main CPU rewrites mq->cache and mq->clk at each turn change (mq_turn_hook). By the values these turn out benign, but the class (cached reads of main-CPU-written memory without an invalidate) is unproven. The ME's digest (xm_list -> gl_digest) is taken from its own cached view before XME_C_ALL, so it would look correct.
hypotheses.evidence_for: PSP only: the emulator has one memory and no separate ME caches. ME turns only.
hypotheses.evidence_against: [C] The step 4d-4 design writes back and invalidates on every hand-over: SYNC dwbinv_all, each post does mq_cpu_wb, a hook end does XME_C_ALL before listed++, entries and extents are invalidated per entry. gl19 on the PSP had ME turns and equalled the twin on 150/150 digests indoors, but digests cannot see this class.
hypotheses.psp_only_why: Separate ME and main-CPU data caches exist only on hardware.
hypotheses.test: Small code change: at mq_submit the main CPU hashes the list words (r->list, the first n words) through the uncached alias and compares with a raw hash the ME stored in XmeRes right after its writeback. Log mismatches per turn. Cost about 1-3 ms a frame, in the window only.
hypotheses.fix: Writeback and invalidate at the points the mismatch names. For example, invalidate the ME's whole cache at the first entry of each ME turn (xme_run, on a turn-start flag).

hypotheses.name: H4 leftover display race (the flip check by vcount misses cases)
hypotheses.mechanism: gl27 holds the next list while sceDisplayGetVcount() == gl_show_vc (mq_service). If the NEXTFRAME latch is not exactly at the vcount increment, the GE can still clear the buffer being scanned. Examples: gl_show running during the vblank interval, or a list whose buffer parity d (gl_built & 1) equals the displayed buffer after a dropped or unshown list.
hypotheses.evidence_for: This was the gl27 theory, and the symptom is unchanged.
hypotheses.evidence_against: [C] gl27 run 2 counted 0 lists drawn into the shown buffer from vb 30,500 with the wait on, and the owner still saw the marks at 23:12. The emulator run with the walk window also counted 0 in every turn (1 hold of 37.5 ms in main turn 31,300).
hypotheses.psp_only_why: PPSSPP draws the list at enqueue, so the screen never scans a buffer the GE is clearing.
hypotheses.test: Small code change: at mq_submit, call sceDisplayGetFrameBuf(&top, ...) and count lists whose target (GL_FB0/GL_FB1) equals the current top, per turn. Also log the vcount at submit minus gl_show_vc.
hypotheses.fix: A third VRAM buffer (480x272x4 = 510 KB; VRAM layout permitting), or sceDisplayWaitVblankStart before the GE clears.

hypotheses.name: H5 real picture content, not PSP-only (missed by the sparse emulator checks)
hypotheses.mechanism: The marks are what the build always draws: the foot splash thinned 1 strip in 2 (MGS2_GL_SPLASH=2), effects not drawn (DEVIATIONS C1: P04+3740 is 38-41% of the aft deck in the rain), draws whose texture is a render target drawn untextured (TK_RT, 181 in gl26), or the lamps at half rate (G1 cut b from vb 24,000). Any of these can appear as dark marks that change with Snake's step or the camera.
hypotheses.evidence_for: [C] The emulator's 'no marks' evidence is 16 pictures in two 7-vblank windows (30,618-30,624, 30,718-30,724) and 3 shots, all under a second of play each. The marks 'come and go every few seconds'. The emulator's frame digests for the deck walk were never checked before my run; gl27's check window 31,561-31,959 is indoors.
hypotheses.evidence_against: The owner noticed it from gl25/gl26 on, but the route and these cuts are older (the splash and C1 date from gl10-gl18). The 3 PSP deck shots show no dark clusters against the emulator.
hypotheses.psp_only_why: It is not PSP-only. The owner has only watched the PSP.
hypotheses.test: Container only: emulator variant with a dense picture dump over 30,500-31,400 (shot_n is capped at 16 in xl_psp.c gl_setup, so a variant build or several runs are needed), scanning each frame for dark clusters. The pictures stay in the container. On the PSP: an on-screen turn marker (or long blocks), then check whether marks appear in main turns and in ME-off blocks too.
hypotheses.fix: Depends on the content. Splash: MGS2_GL_SPLASH=1. Render-target draws: skip instead of drawing untextured. Cut b: MGS2_HALF_CYCLE without 2 (lamps).

hypotheses.name: H6 real-GE rasterization difference (depth precision / decal z-fighting or render-to-self)
hypotheses.mechanism: The frame's depth is remapped per frame from its range (gx_depth_map(map_lo, map_hi)). Coplanar shadow and decal geometry on the deck can z-fight on the real GE's 16-bit depth, flickering as the range changes with the camera. A second possibility is the depth blur, which samples the buffer being drawn (gelive.c gl_tex, kind 2, t.psm = 0) and interacts with the GE's texture cache or alpha/stencil differently from PPSSPP's software renderer.
hypotheses.evidence_for: [C] PSP shots against the emulator: about half the pixels differ by 2 or more ('GE rounding'). The frame digests match, so the input is identical and only the rasterizer differs. Flickering 'shadow-like' marks are what z-fighting looks like.
hypotheses.evidence_against: The 3 PSP deck shots (main turns) have no dark clusters (at most 74 scattered pixels darker by 120+). It does not explain any link to turns.
hypotheses.psp_only_why: The real GE's depth interpolation and texture cache differ from PPSSPP's software rasterizer.
hypotheses.test: Live captures in main-turn and ME-off blocks compared with emulator pictures of the same frames: dark clusters on the PSP only, in every block, with digests equal.
hypotheses.fix: A depth bias or GE depth offset on decal/shadow batches, a fixed or quantized depth range per scene, or turning off the depth blur's render-to-self.

facts: [C] The frame digest is ge/gelive.c gl_digest(f, l) (line 508), called in ge/xlme.c xm_list:359 by whichever CPU makes the frame (the ME in ME turns; the main CPU itself in main turns, through xme_hook) when HOOK.dig is set (psp/xl_psp.c mq_frame: e.h.dig = vb-1 in [dig_from, dig_to]). It hashes the list's own digest l->dig (gelist.c put/put_sym: every list word, addresses as region+offset R_VERT/R_DATA/R_AUX/R_TEX/R_PAL/R_VRAM), counts, the batch table, vertices, data arena, aux block, texture descriptors, and each pool texture's texels and palette. It is taken from the maker's own (cached) view BEFORE XME_C_ALL and before the GE draws, and is printed by the main CPU in mq_submit ('picture: vb N buffer d list L frame F'). So it catches construction differences (late reads, wrong input) but not anything that happens to RAM after listing, GE rasterization, or the display.

[C] The ge/xldig.c (MGS2_GL_DIG's per-call/per-prim 'c'/'v' lines, xdg_*) is the x86 twin's GS-side trace; the PSP digest lines come from gl_digest/gxl.dig, and tools/emucmp.py compares them per vblank with the twin.
